Domain: `domain:cli`
File surface: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/**` (new pins) and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` (the item's `automated.ref`); ⚠️ a pin that genuinely belongs in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`'s own suite widens the declared surface — **declare it and say why**, ⛔ do not take it silently (stop on breach otherwise)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: **no** — tests plus a checklist `automated.ref` re-scope. No runtime behaviour, wire shape or accept/reject decision changes. ⚠️ If pinning a clause requires *changing* an admin route's behaviour, stop and report — that flips the answer.
Serial constraints cleared: **`packages/qa/dogfood/**` is free as of this minute** — sibling #9481 landed `8d982687e` (verified on `origin/main`: both its test files present, and its `automated.ref` re-scope present, 4 references). ⚠️ **Sibling #9483 is deliberately NOT dispatched alongside this card** — it is same-package with this one, and the maintainer re-confirmed on 2026-08-18 (verbatim 「不豁免，维持串行」) that same-package work is not exempted. #9482 goes first because the card marks it **security-priority** per the maintainer's 2026-08-18 approval of the QA landing plan, and because its highest-value clause is a structural guard rather than a point fix.

**Tier derivation** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/qa/dogfood/test/`, run now, ⛔ not recalled): no path-derived mandate. `opus` rather than the `sonnet` floor for the same reason as #9481 — this is an access-control surface, and **a security test that asserts the wrong thing is worse than none**: it converts a known-unpinned gap into a false green that the next Tier-1 run scores as covered.

**Stale-premise check on `origin/main`**: the item is live at `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json:367`, its sole existing pin `admin-identity-audit-trail` exists (covering C8 only, as the card says), and the `/admin/` surface currently comprises **6 routes** — `ban-user`, `impersonate-user`, `remove-user`, `revoke-user-session`, `revoke-user-sessions`, `stop-impersonating`. Those map directly onto the card's clause list (ban persistence, impersonation attribution, revoke-mid-flight, `owner_id` FK clear on removal).

## ⚠️ The design constraint that decides whether this card is worth anything

The card says the route-walking probe is *"exactly the shape that catches a silently unguarded **new** route."* **A probe that hardcodes today's six routes cannot do that** — it would pass forever while route seven ships unguarded, which is the precise failure this lane has already paid for twice (the `#2992` tripwire aimed at the wrong file, and a tripwire keyed off one path spelling instead of transport mechanics, #9409).

⇒ The population must be **derived** — from the router/registration surface — so a newly added `/admin/` route is **automatically in scope and fails until it is guarded**. If deriving it is genuinely impossible, that is a finding to report, and the honest fallback is an enumerated list **plus a count assertion that breaks when the route count changes**, so the pin fails loudly instead of silently under-covering. ⛔ Do not ship a bare hardcoded list.

## State change: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #9652`

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. Paired with the label write and the body edit above — ⛔ a label change without its comment is a half-state.

**PR #9664 is merged** (verified on three readings: timeline `merged`; `origin/main` at `f6c71ead8`; and the probe — both introduced files, `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` and `admin-credential-lifecycle.dogfood.test.ts`, now present against a pre-merge baseline of 0).

### Why this card did NOT close with it

The PR said `Part of #9482`, not `Fixes`. My dispatch brief had asked for `Fixes` — **that was wrong, and the dev was right to override it**:

- AGENTS.md outranks a dispatch brief, and says to use `Part of` when merging should not close the card. The dev followed the standing rule over my instruction *and flagged the conflict* rather than choosing silently.
- The `Part-of PR must not also close its card` gate is green, so this is settled mechanically as well as by rule.
- C0, C3, C4, C5, C6 and C9's allowed half are **named security coverage**. Closing this card on a PR that pins a different subset would retire them on the strength of a checklist note.

### Why `pm:blocked` and not `pm:queue`

The remaining clauses cannot be pinned by *any* test-authoring work. They ride better-auth's own admin endpoints, which authorize on the legacy `user.role === 'admin'` scalar that ADR-0068 D2 deliberately stopped synthesizing — so those routes refuse the platform admin himself. Pinning them requires **changing an admin route's behaviour**, which is a security/authorization boundary decision.

⛔ Not adjudicated by this seat, and not adjudicable by it: #9652 sits on the human floor twice over — an authorization boundary, and its option C would reopen ADR-0068 D2 rather than edit anything. It is for the triage seat to route and the maintainer to rule.

`Blocked-by: #9652` is now line 1 of the body, so the unlock scan returns this card to the queue automatically when that decision lands. ⛔ No `Restart-when:` is needed — this is a real upstream dependency, not a hold.

### Assignee deliberately retained

This lane keeps ownership so the card is re-dispatched here rather than re-triaged from scratch when #9652 rules; `pm:blocked` already removes it from selection, so the assignee is not hiding an available card. Recorded explicitly because a retained assignee on a non-in-flight card is otherwise indistinguishable from a stale claim — and the stale-claim criterion (>~24h, no branch, no PR) ⛔ does not apply here.

## H26 chased one level further: this card's wait is INDEFINITE BY CONSTRUCTION

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`, round 34. The 2026-08-24T08:00Z half-state sweep raised **H26** here — *"the wait is TRANSITIVE: `#9652` is itself `pm:blocked` … this row does not chase the chain; it says to look one level further."* Chasing it, and reporting rather than acting.

**The full chain, read off the same sweep:**

```
#9482  (this card, domain:cli, pm:blocked, parked by this seat)
  └── Blocked-by: #9652  (domain:services, pm:blocked, pm:blocking)
        ├── Blocked-by: #9968  → CLOSED 2026-08-24T03:21:11Z
        └── Blocked-by: #9969  → OPEN, needs-user-decision
```

**#9969 cannot close, and that is not a defect in #9969.** `needs-user-decision` is by definition a state a card occupies *while open* — it is the maintainer's inbox, not a work state. The unlock predicate one hop up is "the `Blocked-by:` target closed". So the release of #9652, and therefore of this card, has **no mechanism that will ever fire**. Every existing gauge passes on the chain: each `Blocked-by:` line is present and well-formed, each target resolves, each label is correct. Nothing is mislabelled anywhere; the wait is simply indefinite by construction.

⚠️ **This is not a claim that the block is wrong.** Waiting on a deferred decision is sometimes exactly right, and #9652's own body is clear that its three options include one (synthesizing `role = 'admin'`) that would reopen ADR-0068 — that genuinely belongs to a person. What the chain means in practice is narrower and worth stating plainly so nobody re-derives it in three weeks:

> **This card moves when, and only when, #9969 is answered.** No sweep, no unlock scan, and no seat can advance it in the meantime.

**Disposition: nothing touched.** `pm:blocked` is correct, the `Blocked-by:` line is correct, and the assignee stays (a parked card keeps the seat that parked it). ⛔ This seat does not touch #9652 or #9969 — one is another lane's card, the other is the maintainer's. The downstream cost has been reported to the services seat on #9652, and #9969 is named in this lane's round report as a decision with a `domain:cli` card behind it. ⛔ Not nagged, and it will not be re-raised until the round report's next natural boundary.

H26 row discharged as report-only.

Branch: `claude/issue-9482-admin-lifecycle-clause-pins`.
Declared file surface: the identity/admin dogfood suites under `packages/qa` + a changeset. Tests only — ⛔ no route behaviour is changed by this card.

## ⛔ First, a correction I owe this card

My comment `5395613493` (13:06Z today) said the chain was **"indefinite by construction"** and that #9652's release had **"no mechanism that will ever fire"**, because `needs-user-decision` is a state a card occupies while open and the unlock predicate is "the target closed".

**That was wrong, and it was falsified within ninety minutes.** #9969 closed **`not_planned`** and #9652 closed completed the same day. A `needs-user-decision` card closing *is* the mechanism — the maintainer answering it is the event, and "answered" can mean closed not_planned just as well as converted to work. I conflated **no automated mechanism** with **no mechanism**, and stated the stronger claim.

⇒ The general lesson, recorded because it is the reusable half: **"no mechanism can fire this" is a claim about the future, and a decision card's whole purpose is to be answered by someone the predicate cannot see.** Do not write off a wait as structurally dead when the thing it waits on is a human decision. Report the wait; ⛔ do not declare it unreachable. (Also corrected in this lane's seat post, which carried the same sentence.)

Credit where due: the release came from the skills seat's `pm:blocking` sweep (`5396675454`), on the maintainer's instruction, and it did the thing my analysis did not — it went and looked at whether the decision had been made.

## What the ruling gives this card — it now knows what to pin

From the release comment, and the reason this is dispatchable rather than merely unblocked:

- **Routes with a real consumer answer `2xx` to platform admins** through ObjectStack raw mounts with the ADR-0068 gate: `ban-user` / `unban-user` (PR #9970); `create-user` / `set-user-password` / `unlock-user` / `import-users` / `oauth2/toggle-disabled` (pre-existing); and the impersonation path now deriving through the consolidated authority `hasPlatformAdminStanding` (PR #11686, merged `7131f12b`).
- **The seven consumer-less routes stay `403` BY DESIGN** — `remove-user`, `revoke-user-session`, `revoke-user-sessions`, `list-user-sessions`, `update-user`, `list-users`, `get-user`. #9969 closed `not_planned` with re-implement-on-demand standing.

⇒ Both sides get asserted. The `403` half is the one that matters most and is easiest to get wrong: it is a **pinned design decision**, not an unasserted gap, so the pin must say so in its own words — otherwise the next author reads a 403 as a bug and "fixes" a deliberate refusal.

⚠️ **Re-verify the route inventory on current `origin/main` at claim time** — #11686's landing is the most recent mover, and the card's own `## Repro` section predates all of it.

**Serial: none.** The lane's other in-flight work is `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts` (#11727), `packages/mcp` (#11622), `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/` (#11733) and `packages/rest` (#11731) — all disjoint from the qa dogfood suites.

**Clause ②:** `no` expected — tests only, no accepted-set change. If pinning turns out to require moving a route's answer, ⛔ **stop and report**: that is the security/authorization boundary this card was parked behind, and it is not re-openable by a tests card.

Standing: worktree first · ⛔ never `git stash` · ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/` · ⛔ do not touch `packages/spec` · every pin red-before/green-after · findings filed **unlabelled** for triage. Draft PR with `Fixes #9482`; ⛔ do not mark ready or arm.
